data-explorer/dashboard.content:
Statistics & Metrics with AI¶

The Dashboard in Schema Weaver turns your raw PostgreSQL database into an executive-grade analytics platform in one click.

Instead of requiring you to write dozens of SQL queries or manually configure BI widgets, Schema Weaver's AI inspects your schema, detects core business entities, calculates growth drivers, and generates interactive charts, metric cards, and written executive recommendations tailored to your business.

Quick links: Exploring Your Data · Resona Dashboard AI · Connector Setup

1 — Generating a Dashboard from Scratch¶

When you connect a new PostgreSQL database and switch to Dashboard mode, you are greeted with the initial setup view:

How AI analyzes and builds your dashboard¶

When you click Generate <database> Dashboard → (or + Create Dashboard in the sidebar), the AI follows an autonomous 5-step analysis pipeline:

  1. Schema & Relationship Mapping: AI inspects your database structure, table definitions, foreign keys, and relationships to map how your business domain is modeled.
  2. Core Business Metric Discovery: AI identifies key revenue drivers, user registration flows, order transactions, customer engagement habits, and growth trajectories.
  3. Safe, Read-Only Execution: AI analyzes your live database using strictly controlled, read-only SQL queries through the connector. No data is ever mutated or written.
  4. Synthesis into Executive KPIs & Trends: Raw aggregations are synthesized into top-level KPIs, growth trends, segment cohorts, and written strategic narratives.
  5. Interactive Executive Presentation: Delivers a multi-section dashboard with live charts, drill-downs, and proactive AI recommendations ready for team review.

2 — The Generated Dashboard Layout¶

Once generated, your dashboard organizes your metrics into clean, thematic sections with a rich variety of visualization cards:

Left Sidebar Sections¶

The sidebar automatically clusters related analytics into dedicated navigation sections (e.g. SECTIONS (7)):

  • Overview: High-level executive summary of key performance indicators.
  • Growth & Acquisition (e.g. Learner Growth): Weekly signups, cumulative user totals, and activation curves.
  • Outcomes & Performance (e.g. Learning Outcomes): Core user achievements, scores, and completion metrics.
  • Engagement & Sessions: Session frequency, activity heatmaps, and retention.
  • Platform & Infrastructure Cost (e.g. AI Platform & Cost): Operational resource utilization, token consumption, and model expenses.
  • Directory Lists: Top users, power users, and account tables.
  • Executive Analysis: Written executive summaries and diagnostic insights.

Use the search icon to filter sections, or collapse the sidebar at any time to expand the canvas.

Visualization Card Types¶

Card TypeWhat it displaysExample in Dashboard
Line ChartTemporal volume trends and cycle fluctuationsWEEKLY NEW SIGNUPS
Area ChartCumulative growth and running lifetime volumeCUMULATIVE LEARNER BASE
Donut ChartProportional segment distribution across categoriesLEARNERS BY GRADE
Bar ChartCategorical comparisons and discrete frequency binsLEARNERS BY BOARD
KPI MetricHeadline value with period-over-period delta badgesGrowth % and active user counts
Executive ReadWritten strategic diagnosis with action recommendationsEngagement ratios and quality risks

3 — Executive Analysis & Actionable Insights¶

Dashboards in Schema Weaver go beyond passive charts by generating Executive Read cards that interpret what the data actually means and prescribe what action your team should take next:

Structure of an Executive Read Card¶

Each insight card is structured for executive decision-making:

  • Headline Metric: The focal number anchoring the analysis (e.g., 494, 79.4%, 28).
  • Trend Delta: Period-over-period percentage shift (e.g., • 0.0%).
  • Diagnostic Narrative: Plain-English explanation detailing the underlying cause. For example:

    "79% of everything learners type is a correction of the tutor: 392 of 494 learner messages are 'user_correction', sent by 24 of the 31 learners who chat... Only 100 messages are genuine learner questions — learners are doing the tutor's quality control instead of learning from it."

  • Actionable Next Step: Concrete tactical advice you can implement immediately:

    Next step Instrument the correction stream first: sample and classify the 392 corrections, then patch the 2-3 recurring error classes in the tutor prompt/knowledge base. Cutting corrections by 30% removes ~118 tutoring-the-tutor turns per cycle and hands that time back to actual learning.

  • Classification Badges: Categorizes the finding (e.g., ENGAGEMENT_INSIGHT, TUTOR_QUALITY_RISK).
  • Confidence Rating: AI certainty assessment (e.g., HIGH CONFIDENCE).
  • "Why?" Drill-Down: Click the Why? button to view the underlying SQL queries, sample distributions, and statistical reasoning behind the recommendation.

4 — Managing Panels & Card Operations¶

Every card on the dashboard includes individual management controls accessible via the ... menu in the card header:

Available Panel Operations:¶

OperationAction
RefreshRe-executes the individual card's SQL query to fetch the freshest database data without reloading the entire dashboard.
Focus ModeExpands the selected card into a maximized fullscreen modal for presentations and deep data inspection.
Resize WidthToggles the card's grid footprint between standard half-width and full-width layout.
CollapseMinimizes the card body while keeping the title bar visible to save vertical canvas space.
Move Left / RightShifts the card's position earlier or later in the dashboard grid order.
Hide CardTemporarily hides the card from the view without permanently deleting its query definition.
Delete CardPermanently removes the card and its associated query from the dashboard.

5 — Resona Dashboard AI¶

The dashboard is fully interactive and conversational. By opening the Resona Dashboard AI side panel (or using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl / Cmd + J), you can collaborate with your dedicated live analytics partner:

Conversational Dashboard Editing¶

You don't need to manually configure queries or write SQL to modify your dashboard. Simply tell Dashboard AI what you want to see:

  • Create new cards:

    "Add a chart showing monthly churn rate segmented by subscription tier"

  • Refine existing charts:

    "Show weekly signups grouped by referral channel instead of total counts"

  • Diagnose business anomalies:

    "What are our primary revenue drivers and growth trends?" "Summarize overall business health and customer retention" "Highlight key executive KPIs and weekly performance"

  • Restructure layouts:

    "Move the revenue cohort section to the top of the Overview" "Remove the legacy staging cards"

Flash vs. Deep Mode¶

Toggle between analysis modes at the bottom of the Dashboard AI chat:

  • Flash Mode: Fast, single-table metrics and direct layout modifications.
  • Deep Mode: Comprehensive multi-table joins, historical cohort comparisons, and complex statistical trend discovery.

Read-Only Security & Team Sharing¶

  • Strict Read-Only Execution: All dashboard operations and AI queries run through your local Connector in read-only mode. Production tables can never be altered or updated.
  • Shared with Your Team: Once generated, your dashboard is accessible to all team members linked to the connection. Teammates can view, filter, and refresh cards without using extra AI credits.

Next Steps¶

  • Exploring Your Data — inspect raw rows in the Data Explorer grid
  • Exporting Data — download views and charts to CSV, Sheets, Excel, or JSON
  • Resona AI Chat — run deep ad-hoc natural language data analyses
  • The Connector — verify database connectivity and live health

data-explorer/exploring-data.content:
Exploring Your Data¶

With a connection selected, you get a two-panel layout — a sidebar of tables on the left, a data grid on the right. Connections come from the Connector and are available here automatically.

The sidebar¶

With a connection active, the left sidebar displays all discoverable database schemas and tables.

  • Schema selector — Switch between any schema in your database (public, analytics, audit, inventory, staging, etc.), defaulting to public. Switching schemas dynamically reloads the table list.
  • Searchable table list — Filter tables with the Filter tables... search input, which displays a live count badge (e.g. 59 tables).
  • Row counts & indicators — Each table item shows an estimated row count badge (e.g., admin_chat 2.2K, ai_token_logs 31.0K) so you can gauge size at a glance.
  • Collapsible sidebar — Click the collapse toggle icon in the top right of the sidebar header to hide the sidebar and give your data grid maximum horizontal screen space.

Smart column sizing¶

Columns size themselves to fit your actual data, measured with the browser's canvas text renderer so the widths match what you see.

How it works¶

  1. Measured, not guessed — text widths are measured using the same font the cell renders in
  2. Sampled from real rows — the first 8 rows of the current page are measured and the widest value sets the column width
  3. A minimum applies to every column — a column is never narrower than its header needs, with a 100px floor so key and type labels always fit
  4. A maximum applies by type, so a long text value can't push a numeric column out of shape:
Column typeMaximum width
Boolean110px
Integer, numeric, float160px
Date, time, timestamp200px
UUID280px
Text and everything else450px

Changing a width¶

Drag the right edge of a header to resize, or double-click the edge to reset it to the calculated width.

Widths you set are remembered per connection, schema, and table, so a table you tuned stays tuned. Writes are debounced while you drag, and the most recently used 50 table layouts are kept.

Sorting¶

Click the sort control on any column header to cycle:

  1. Ascending
  2. Descending
  3. Off — back to the default order

Sorting runs in the database, so it stays fast on large tables. Changing the sort returns you to the first page.

Filtering¶

Click Filter in the grid toolbar to open the filter popover.

Dual-mode filtering¶

Schema Weaver supports two complementary filtering strategies:

  1. Instant In-Memory Filtering (Default)

    • Indicated by the green Instant In-Memory badge in the popover header.
    • Evaluates filter conditions instantaneously on the client side across all rows currently loaded in your browser memory (e.g., your active 500, 1k, or 2k rows).
    • Provides instant, zero-latency typing feedback with no roundtrip database latency — ideal for rapid exploratory analysis on the loaded page.

  2. Query Entire Database

    • Check the Query entire database checkbox.
    • Translates your condition into a server-side SQL WHERE clause and executes it against the live PostgreSQL database through your connector.
    • Scans the entire table (even across millions of rows), fetching and displaying matching records regardless of whether they were in your initial page memory.

Supported operators¶

Column typeOperators
Text~ Contains, Does not contain, Starts with, Ends with, Is empty, =, ≠
Number=, ≠, >, ≥, <, ≤
Boolean=, ≠
Date / time=, ≠, >, ≥, <, ≤
Any typeIn list, Is null, Not null

Active filters appear as dismissible chips in the action bar. Remove any single filter by clicking its ✕ button, or click Clear all to reset the view.

Columns¶

The Columns button allows you to control which fields appear in your grid view.

  • Visibility counter — The button label dynamically tracks your active column ratio (e.g. Columns (12 / 12 visible)).
  • Column search — Quickly filter through wide tables using the Search columns... search box.
  • Data type indicators — Lists PostgreSQL data types alongside each column name (integer, character varying(50), text, text[], etc.).
  • Convenient presets:
    • Show all: Instantly restores visibility for all columns.
    • Hide except PK: One-click action to hide every column except the primary key (id), giving you a clean baseline to add back only the specific fields you need.
  • Persistent preferences: Your visibility choices are stored per connection, schema, and table so your customized layouts remain intact when you return.

Column statistics¶

Click a column header — not the sort control — to open the stats panel for that column.

StatWhat it shows
TypeFull data type, with a nullable marker
FlagsPrimary key and indexed badges
Null %How much of the column is empty
Distinct countHow many unique values
Min / maxRange, for numbers and dates
CompletenessA bar showing the non-null share
Top valuesMost frequent values with their share
Sample valuesA quick look at real values

Close it with the X, or by clicking the same header again.

Click to copy¶

Click any cell to copy its value directly. A brief Copied badge confirms the action.

Cell valueCopied as
NULLNULL
Booleantrue or false
JSONPretty-printed
DateISO 8601
TextAs shown

Cell hover preview & inspector¶

Long strings, multi-sentence messages, JSON structures, and arrays are truncated with an ellipsis (...) in the grid to maintain compact row heights. Rather than requiring you to expand columns, drag headers, or open a separate modal, Schema Weaver includes an instant cell hover preview:

Key capabilities:¶

  • Instant zero-click inspection: Hover over any truncated cell in any column to immediately read the complete, unclipped text.
  • Context details: The popover header shows the target column name (e.g. message), data type badge (text), and row reference (Row #7).
  • Quick actions:
    • Copy: Copy the complete unclipped text to your clipboard with a single click.
    • Expand: Enlarge the floating card for lengthy paragraphs or complex documents.
    • Full inspector: Jump to the comprehensive cell inspector modal for nested JSON tree inspection or multi-line formatting.
  • Character count: Displays the exact length of the cell value (e.g., 276 chars).
  • Keyboard friendly: Press Esc anytime to instantly dismiss the preview card.

Pagination & page fetch limits¶

The grid uses high-performance cursor pagination to seamlessly page through massive PostgreSQL tables. You can customize how many rows are fetched into memory per page using the Rows per page selector in the grid toolbar:

Rows per page options:¶

  • 100 / page — Minimal memory footprint for mobile or slower connections
  • 250 / page — Standard responsive scrolling
  • 500 / page (Default) — Recommended sweet spot for performance and in-memory exploration
  • 1000 / page (1k) — Broader working set for batch review
  • 2000 / page (2k) — Maximum batch fetch for deep client-side in-memory filtering across thousands of rows

The bottom status bar displays your current position alongside an estimated total row count (e.g. Showing 500 of ~2.0K rows). Because paging is cursor-based, moving forward through millions of rows stays instantaneous.

Keyboard shortcut¶

ShortcutAction
Ctrl / Cmd + JOpen or close the Dashboard AI panel

Everything else in the grid is pointer-driven: click a cell to copy, click a header to sort or open statistics, drag a header edge to resize.

Next Steps¶

  • Exporting Data — take the grid to CSV, Sheets, Excel, JSON, or SQL
  • Resona AI — ask questions about what you're looking at
  • Data Explorer — back to the overview

- **Convenient presets**:
  - **Show all**: Instantly restores visibility for all columns.
  - **Hide except PK**: One-click action to hide every column except the primary key (`id`), giving you a clean baseline to add back only the specific fields you need.
- **Persistent preferences**: Your visibility choices are stored per connection, schema, and table so your customized layouts remain intact when you return.

---

## Column statistics

Click a **column header** — not the sort control — to open the stats panel for that column.

| Stat | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Full data type, with a nullable marker |
| **Flags** | Primary key and indexed badges |
| **Null %** | How much of the column is empty |
| **Distinct count** | How many unique values |
| **Min / max** | Range, for numbers and dates |
| **Completeness** | A bar showing the non-null share |
| **Top values** | Most frequent values with their share |
| **Sample values** | A quick look at real values |

Close it with the X, or by clicking the same header again.

---

## Click to copy

Click any cell to copy its value directly. A brief **Copied** badge confirms the action.

| Cell value | Copied as |
|---|---|
| `NULL` | `NULL` |
| Boolean | `true` or `false` |
| JSON | Pretty-printed |
| Date | ISO 8601 |
| Text | As shown |

---

## Cell hover preview & inspector

Long strings, multi-sentence messages, JSON structures, and arrays are truncated with an ellipsis (`...`) in the grid to maintain compact row heights. Rather than requiring you to expand columns, drag headers, or open a separate modal, Schema Weaver includes an **instant cell hover preview**:

![Cell hover preview popover in Schema Weaver Data Explorer showing complete unclipped text content, character count, and full inspector shortcut](/images/de/de-grid/hover-full-message.png)

### Key capabilities:

- **Instant zero-click inspection**: Hover over any truncated cell in any column to immediately read the complete, unclipped text.
- **Context details**: The popover header shows the target column name (e.g. `message`), data type badge (`text`), and row reference (`Row #7`).
- **Quick actions**:
  - **Copy**: Copy the complete unclipped text to your clipboard with a single click.
  - **Expand**: Enlarge the floating card for lengthy paragraphs or complex documents.
  - **Full inspector**: Jump to the comprehensive cell inspector modal for nested JSON tree inspection or multi-line formatting.
- **Character count**: Displays the exact length of the cell value (e.g., `276 chars`).
- **Keyboard friendly**: Press `Esc` anytime to instantly dismiss the preview card.

---

## Pagination & page fetch limits

The grid uses high-performance cursor pagination to seamlessly page through massive PostgreSQL tables. You can customize how many rows are fetched into memory per page using the **Rows per page** selector in the grid toolbar:

![Page size selector dropdown in Schema Weaver Data Explorer showing 100, 250, 500, 1000, and 2000 rows per page options](/images/de/de-grid/page.png)

### Rows per page options:

- **100 / page** — Minimal memory footprint for mobile or slower connections
- **250 / page** — Standard responsive scrolling
- **500 / page** (Default) — Recommended sweet spot for performance and in-memory exploration
- **1000 / page (1k)** — Broader working set for batch review
- **2000 / page (2k)** — Maximum batch fetch for deep client-side in-memory filtering across thousands of rows

The bottom status bar displays your current position alongside an estimated total row count (e.g. `Showing 500 of ~2.0K rows`). Because paging is cursor-based, moving forward through millions of rows stays instantaneous.

---

## Keyboard shortcut

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl` / `Cmd` + `J` | Open or close the Dashboard AI panel |

Everything else in the grid is pointer-driven: click a cell to copy, click a header to sort or open statistics, drag a header edge to resize.

---

## Next Steps

- [Exporting Data](/data-explorer/exporting-data) — take the grid to CSV, Sheets, Excel, JSON, or SQL
- [Resona AI](/resona-ai) — ask questions about what you're looking at
- [Data Explorer](/data-explorer) — back to the overview

data-explorer/exporting-data.content:
Exporting Data¶

Anything you can see in the Data Explorer, you can take with you. Export the exact view you're looking at, one or many tables, or every table in a schema bundled into a single ZIP — as CSV, Google Sheets, Excel, JSON, or SQL.

Export formats¶

FormatBest for
CSVSpreadsheets, BI tools, scripts
Google SheetsShared spreadsheets
ExcelFormatted Excel workbooks
JSONApps and API payloads
SQLReplaying into another database

These are the same icons you see in the export popover, so you can match a format to its icon at a glance.

The three export scopes¶

Not sure which format? Pick what you want to take with you first — the Export button in the top-right of the Data Explorer lets you choose the scope before you choose the format.

ScopeWhat you getGrid state applied?
ViewExactly what you're looking at — current filters, sort order, and visible columnsYes
TableFull data for one or more tables you selectNo
DatabaseEvery table in one or more schemas, bundled as a ZIP archiveNo

1. View Scope — WYSIWYG Grid Export¶

The View tab exports the current grid state exactly as you have configured it on screen.

  • Active View Summary: Anchored to the active table (e.g. public.admin_chat) with an Active View badge.
  • Grid Dimensions: Displays estimated visible rows (e.g., ~500 rows) and column count (12/12 columns).
  • Preserved State: Retains all active filter conditions, column sorting orders, and hidden column configurations.
  • Safety Limit: Select a row cap (default 10k rows).
  • Action: Click Export View () to download your formatted export immediately.

2. Table Scope — Targeted Table Selection¶

The Table tab allows you to export raw, unfiltered data from one or more selected tables within the active schema.

  • Search & Filter: Use the Filter tables... search input to quickly isolate tables in large schemas.
  • Checklist & Select All: Select individual tables or click Select all to batch export multiple tables.
  • Row Estimates: Shows live row count estimates directly next to each table (e.g. admin_chat ~1962, ai_token_logs ~30984).
  • Selection Summary: The footer displays total selected tables and schema name (e.g., 1 table selected (admin_chat), Schema: public).
  • Unfiltered Data: Unlike the View scope, Table exports bypass UI filters and sorts to export the canonical table data.

3. Database Scope — Multi-Schema ZIP Archive¶

The Database tab bundles all tables across your selected schemas into a single, downloadable .zip archive.

  • All Schemas Checklist: Toggle All schemas (63 tables) or check individual schemas (e.g. public (21), analytics (2), audit (1), inventory (1), staging (1)).
  • Format Selection: Choose between CSV, Excel, JSON, or SQL for every table in the archive.
  • Archive Structure: Packages each table into an individual file inside the ZIP archive (e.g., schema_export_2026-04-04.zip).
  • Google Sheets Note: Google Sheets is disabled for multi-schema ZIP archives because it requires creating individual cloud documents.

This distinction between scopes matters: View is WYSIWYG, while Table and Database exports ignore filters and sorts to export complete datasets.

Row limits¶

Exports are capped so a single request can't run away on a large table.

PresetRows
1k rows1,000
5k rows5,000
10k rows10,000 — default
25k rows25,000
50k rows50,000

The default is 10,000 rows per table. Pick a higher preset if you need more — the limit is applied server-side, so a larger export simply takes longer.

If your export hits the cap you'll see a confirmation noting it, for example "Capped at 10,000 rows."

Database (ZIP) exports ignore the row limit. The limit only applies to the View and Table scopes. For a full-schema export, the backend decides how much it writes per table.

Google Sheets export¶

Google Sheets creates a spreadsheet directly in your Drive and hands you a link to it.

  1. Select Google Sheets as your format.
  2. Click the export button.
  3. Sign in to Google when prompted and approve access.
  4. Your spreadsheet opens in a new tab, and a link is also shown in the export panel.

A few things worth knowing:

  • Requested permission is drive.file — Schema Weaver can only create files. It cannot read, edit, or delete anything else in your Drive.
  • Authorization is remembered for about an hour, so you won't be prompted on every export. Expired authorization re-prompts automatically on the next attempt.
  • Sheet names follow schema.table (YYYY-MM-DD), for example public.users (2026-04-04).
  • Recent Sheets exports are listed inside the export panel, so you can jump back to a spreadsheet you created earlier without re-exporting.
  • Not available for the Database scope. Google Sheets is disabled for ZIP exports — pick CSV, Excel, JSON, or SQL for those.

Choosing tables and schemas¶

Table scope lists every table in the current schema. Search the list when it gets long, and use the checkbox to select several tables at once. The panel footer shows how many are selected and, for a single table, which one.

Database scope lets you pick which schemas to include. By default all schemas that contain tables are included; untick individual schemas to narrow it down, or untick everything except one to export a single schema.

File names¶

ScopeHow the name is built
View / TableSet by the server from the table name and format
Database (ZIP)An archive containing one file per table — for example schema_export_2026-04-04.zip
Google Sheetsschema.table (YYYY-MM-DD)

Export states¶

SituationWhat happens
No connection selectedExport is disabled
No table selectedView is unavailable; Database opens by default
No tables selected in Table scopeExport button disabled
Sheets selected with Database scopeExport button disabled, with an inline note explaining why
Export in progressButton shows a spinner and a progress counter; inputs are locked
Export cancelledA confirmation appears
Export failedAn error appears and the export panel stays open so you can retry
Some tables in a multi-table export failedThe confirmation reports how many succeeded

Export from an AI artifact¶

Data tables and reports produced by Resona AI have their own export action in the artifact toolbar — separate from the grid export described above.

Use cases¶

Hand a result to someone else

Export the View scope after filtering and sorting — the file contains exactly the question you asked, with no extra rows to trim.

Load into a notebook

JSON for pandas, R, or Jupyter. Point your loader at the downloaded file.

Move data between environments

Export as SQL and replay the statements in another database.

Note: the SQL export contains INSERT INTO statements for the data only — it does not include table definitions. Create the schema first, then replay the inserts.

Snapshot a whole environment

Export every schema as a ZIP on a schedule and keep the archives as dated backups.

Next Steps¶

  • Exploring Your Data — filtering, sorting, and column statistics
  • Resona AI — exporting results from an AI analysis
  • Security Architecture — where exported data goes

# Exporting Data

Anything you can see in the Data Explorer, you can take with you. Export the exact view you're looking at, one or many tables, or every table in a schema bundled into a single ZIP — as **CSV, Google Sheets, Excel, JSON, or SQL**.

---

## Export formats

| | Format | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| ![CSV](/images/data-explorer/formats/csv.svg) | **CSV** | Spreadsheets, BI tools, scripts |
| ![Google Sheets](/images/data-explorer/formats/google-sheets.svg) | **Google Sheets** | Shared spreadsheets |
| ![Excel](/images/data-explorer/formats/excel.svg) | **Excel** | Formatted Excel workbooks |
| ![JSON](/images/data-explorer/formats/json.svg) | **JSON** | Apps and API payloads |
| ![SQL](/images/data-explorer/formats/sql.svg) | **SQL** | Replaying into another database |

These are the same icons you see in the export popover, so you can match a format to its icon at a glance.

---

## The three export scopes

Not sure which format? Pick what you want to take with you first — the **Export** button in the top-right of the Data Explorer lets you choose the scope before you choose the format.

| Scope | What you get | Grid state applied? |
|---|---|---|
| **View** | Exactly what you're looking at — current filters, sort order, and visible columns | Yes |
| **Table** | Full data for one or more tables you select | No |
| **Database** | Every table in one or more schemas, bundled as a ZIP archive | No |

---

### 1. View Scope — WYSIWYG Grid Export

The **View** tab exports the current grid state exactly as you have configured it on screen.

![Export View popover in Schema Weaver Data Explorer showing active view summary, row count, column dimensions, format selector, and row limits](/images/de/export/view-export.png)

- **Active View Summary**: Anchored to the active table (e.g. `public.admin_chat`) with an `Active View` badge.
- **Grid Dimensions**: Displays estimated visible rows (e.g., `~500 rows`) and column count (`12/12 columns`).
- **Preserved State**: Retains all active filter conditions, column sorting orders, and hidden column configurations.
- **Safety Limit**: Select a row cap (default `10k rows`).
- **Action**: Click **Export View (<Format>)** to download your formatted export immediately.

---

### 2. Table Scope — Targeted Table Selection

The **Table** tab allows you to export raw, unfiltered data from one or more selected tables within the active schema.

![Table Export popover showing multi-table selection checkboxes, live search filter, estimated row counts, format options, and row limits](/images/de/export/table-export.png)

- **Search & Filter**: Use the `Filter tables...` search input to quickly isolate tables in large schemas.
- **Checklist & Select All**: Select individual tables or click **Select all** to batch export multiple tables.
- **Row Estimates**: Shows live row count estimates directly next to each table (e.g. `admin_chat ~1962`, `ai_token_logs ~30984`).
- **Selection Summary**: The footer displays total selected tables and schema name (e.g., `1 table selected (admin_chat)`, `Schema: public`).
- **Unfiltered Data**: Unlike the View scope, Table exports bypass UI filters and sorts to export the canonical table data.

---

### 3. Database Scope — Multi-Schema ZIP Archive

The **Database** tab bundles all tables across your selected schemas into a single, downloadable `.zip` archive.

![Full Database Export popover showing schema checklist with table counts, format options, and Export Database as ZIP action](/images/de/export/database-full-export.png)

- **All Schemas Checklist**: Toggle **All schemas** (`63 tables`) or check individual schemas (e.g. `public (21)`, `analytics (2)`, `audit (1)`, `inventory (1)`, `staging (1)`).
- **Format Selection**: Choose between CSV, Excel, JSON, or SQL for every table in the archive.
- **Archive Structure**: Packages each table into an individual file inside the ZIP archive (e.g., `schema_export_2026-04-04.zip`).
- **Google Sheets Note**: Google Sheets is disabled for multi-schema ZIP archives because it requires creating individual cloud documents.

This distinction between scopes matters: **View** is WYSIWYG, while **Table** and **Database** exports ignore filters and sorts to export complete datasets.

---

## Row limits

Exports are capped so a single request can't run away on a large table.

| Preset | Rows |
|---|---|
| 1k rows | 1,000 |
| 5k rows | 5,000 |
| **10k rows** | **10,000 — default** |
| 25k rows | 25,000 |
| 50k rows | 50,000 |

The default is **10,000 rows per table**. Pick a higher preset if you need more — the limit is applied server-side, so a larger export simply takes longer.

If your export hits the cap you'll see a confirmation noting it, for example *"Capped at 10,000 rows."*

> **Database (ZIP) exports ignore the row limit.** The limit only applies to the **View** and **Table** scopes. For a full-schema export, the backend decides how much it writes per table.

---

## Google Sheets export

Google Sheets creates a spreadsheet directly in your Drive and hands you a link to it.

1. Select **Google Sheets** as your format.
2. Click the export button.
3. Sign in to Google when prompted and approve access.
4. Your spreadsheet opens in a new tab, and a link is also shown in the export panel.

A few things worth knowing:

- **Requested permission is `drive.file`** — Schema Weaver can only create files. It cannot read, edit, or delete anything else in your Drive.
- **Authorization is remembered** for about an hour, so you won't be prompted on every export. Expired authorization re-prompts automatically on the next attempt.
- **Sheet names** follow `schema.table (YYYY-MM-DD)`, for example `public.users (2026-04-04)`.
- **Recent Sheets exports** are listed inside the export panel, so you can jump back to a spreadsheet you created earlier without re-exporting.
- **Not available for the Database scope.** Google Sheets is disabled for ZIP exports — pick CSV, Excel, JSON, or SQL for those.

---

## Choosing tables and schemas

**Table scope** lists every table in the current schema. Search the list when it gets long, and use the checkbox to select several tables at once. The panel footer shows how many are selected and, for a single table, which one.

**Database scope** lets you pick which schemas to include. By default all schemas that contain tables are included; untick individual schemas to narrow it down, or untick everything except one to export a single schema.

---

## File names

| Scope | How the name is built |
|---|---|
| **View / Table** | Set by the server from the table name and format |
| **Database (ZIP)** | An archive containing one file per table — for example `schema_export_2026-04-04.zip` |
| **Google Sheets** | `schema.table (YYYY-MM-DD)` |

---

## Export states

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| No connection selected | **Export** is disabled |
| No table selected | **View** is unavailable; **Database** opens by default |
| No tables selected in Table scope | Export button disabled |
| Sheets selected with Database scope | Export button disabled, with an inline note explaining why |
| Export in progress | Button shows a spinner and a progress counter; inputs are locked |
| Export cancelled | A confirmation appears |
| Export failed | An error appears and the export panel stays open so you can retry |
| Some tables in a multi-table export failed | The confirmation reports how many succeeded |

---

## Export from an AI artifact

Data tables and reports produced by Resona AI have their own export action in the artifact toolbar — separate from the grid export described above.

---

## Use cases

**Hand a result to someone else**

Export the **View** scope after filtering and sorting — the file contains exactly the question you asked, with no extra rows to trim.

**Load into a notebook**

JSON for pandas, R, or Jupyter. Point your loader at the downloaded file.

**Move data between environments**

Export as SQL and replay the statements in another database.

> **Note:** the SQL export contains `INSERT INTO` statements for the data only — it does not include table definitions. Create the schema first, then replay the inserts.

**Snapshot a whole environment**

Export every schema as a ZIP on a schedule and keep the archives as dated backups.

---

- [Resona AI](/resona-ai) — exporting results from an AI analysis
- [Security Architecture](/connector/security-architecture) — where exported data goes

data-explorer.content:
Data Explorer¶

The Data Explorer is where you work with live data. Connect a PostgreSQL database and you can browse it, ask it questions, or talk to it out loud.

Three ways to work¶

Three top-level modes — move between them at any time without losing your place.

ModeWhat it's for
Data ExplorerRead raw data in a high-performance grid — filter, sort, inspect
Resona AIAn autonomous agent that deep-dives your data and writes the report
DashboardOne click, and it builds the executive dashboard from your database

Explore your data¶

Every table in your database, in a grid built for large ones. Filter with instant in-memory search or full database queries, customize page fetch sizes (from 100 to 2k rows), hover over any cell to read the full unclipped message or JSON without expanding, and inspect column statistics with a single click.

→ Exploring Your Data

Ask Resona AI¶

Resona is the assistant throughout Schema Weaver. It comes in a different form depending on where you are:

AgentWhere it livesWhat it's for
ResonaFull panel in Resona AI modeYour main analyst — ask anything, get answers and files back
Dashboard AIPanel beside your dashboardBuilds the dashboard and explains what each metric means
VoiceA floating orb, over every modeAsk out loud instead of typing

Depth is your choice — Flash for quick questions, Deep for multi-table analysis.

The voice orb is the one that follows you: start a session in the grid and it's still running when you switch to a chat or a dashboard.

→ Resona AI

Build a dashboard¶

One click and Schema Weaver reads your database, works out which metrics matter, and builds the executive dashboard — KPI cards, growth curves, segment distributions, and written actionable insights. Shared with your team automatically.

→ Statistics & Metrics with AI

Export your data¶

Export with three distinct scopes: the current view (WYSIWYG with active filters and sorting), selected tables, or a full database schema bundled into a ZIP archive.

→ Exporting Data

Read-only by design¶

The connector authenticates locally and rejects anything that would modify your database, so exploring can never mutate production — whatever the AI generates. Your credentials never leave your environment.

→ Security Architecture

Before you start¶

You need a PostgreSQL connection. Schema Weaver reaches your database through a connector that runs inside your environment, so it never holds your credentials.

→ Install & Run

Next Steps¶

  • Exploring Your Data — the grid, filters, sorting, and column statistics
  • Exporting Data — formats, scopes, and row limits
  • Statistics & Metrics with AI — executive dashboard, written insights, and Dashboard AI
  • Resona AI — what the agent can do for you
  • Workspace & Projects — organising your analyses
  • Security Architecture — credentials, read-only enforcement, and the data plane

# Data Explorer

The Data Explorer is where you work with live data. Connect a PostgreSQL database and you can browse it, ask it questions, or talk to it out loud.

---

## Three ways to work

Three top-level modes — move between them at any time without losing your place.

| Mode | What it's for |
|---|---|
| **Data Explorer** | Read raw data in a high-performance grid — filter, sort, inspect |
| **Resona AI** | An autonomous agent that deep-dives your data and writes the report |
| **Dashboard** | One click, and it builds the executive dashboard from your database |

---

## Explore your data

Every table in your database, in a grid built for large ones. Filter with instant in-memory search or full database queries, customize page fetch sizes (from 100 to 2k rows), hover over any cell to read the full unclipped message or JSON without expanding, and inspect column statistics with a single click.

→ [Exploring Your Data](/data-explorer/exploring-data)

---

## Ask Resona AI

![Resona AI in Data Explorer with natural-language prompt bar, table suggestion chips, and voice launch shortcut](/images/de/resona-ai/de/de.png)

Resona is the assistant throughout Schema Weaver. It comes in a different form depending on where you are:

| Agent | Where it lives | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| **Resona** | Full panel in Resona AI mode | Your main analyst — ask anything, get answers and files back |
| **Dashboard AI** | Panel beside your dashboard | Builds the dashboard and explains what each metric means |
| **Voice** | A floating orb, over every mode | Ask out loud instead of typing |

Depth is your choice — **Flash** for quick questions, **Deep** for multi-table analysis.

The voice orb is the one that follows you: start a session in the grid and it's still running when you switch to a chat or a dashboard.

→ [Resona AI](/resona-ai)

---

## Build a dashboard

![Schema Weaver Dashboard mode displaying executive business metrics, learner growth curves, and category breakdowns](/images/de/dashabord/dashbord.png)

One click and Schema Weaver reads your database, works out which metrics matter, and builds the executive dashboard — KPI cards, growth curves, segment distributions, and written actionable insights. Shared with your team automatically.

→ [Statistics & Metrics with AI](/data-explorer/dashboard)

---

## Export your data

![Schema Weaver Data Explorer export popover showing format and scope options](/images/de/export/view-export.png)

| | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ![CSV](/images/data-explorer/formats/csv.svg) | ![Google Sheets](/images/data-explorer/formats/google-sheets.svg) | ![Excel](/images/data-explorer/formats/excel.svg) | ![JSON](/images/data-explorer/formats/json.svg) | ![SQL](/images/data-explorer/formats/sql.svg) |

Export with three distinct scopes: the **current view** (WYSIWYG with active filters and sorting), **selected tables**, or a **full database schema** bundled into a ZIP archive.

→ [Exporting Data](/data-explorer/exporting-data)

---

## Read-only by design

The connector authenticates locally and rejects anything that would modify your database, so exploring can never mutate production — whatever the AI generates. Your credentials never leave your environment.

→ [Security Architecture](/connector/security-architecture)

---

## Before you start

You need a PostgreSQL connection. Schema Weaver reaches your database through a connector that runs inside your environment, so it never holds your credentials.

→ [Install & Run](/connector/install)

resona-ai/ai-chat.content:
Chat Interface¶

Resona's primary conversational surface in the Data Explorer. Ask a question in plain English, and it autonomously inspects your schema, writes optimized SQL, executes read-only queries through your local connector, and answers with interactive results or downloadable deliverables.

Quick links: Data Explorer Overview · Resona Voice · Dashboard AI · Workspace & Projects

1 — Workspace & Interface Overview¶

The Resona AI surface is purpose-built for fast data exploration:

  • Sidebar & History:
    • + New chat: Start a fresh conversation with a clean slate anytime.
    • Projects & Artifacts: Group sessions into shared workspaces and access all previously generated files.
    • YOUR CHATS: Full session history with relative timestamps (5d ago, 7d ago) for instant resumption.
    • Bottom Switcher: Jump seamlessly between Explorer (table grid) and Dashboard without losing conversation context.
  • Context Header:
    • Live breadcrumb tracking the active connection, schema, and table (e.g., cloopdb > public > admin_chat).
    • Top-right Export button for rapid data exports.
  • One-Click Table Chips:
    • Pre-populated starter chips (such as @admin_chat overview, @ai_token_logs overview) let you trigger comprehensive table profiling with a single click.
  • Unified Input Bar:
    • + Attach files: Upload external reference spreadsheets, PDFs, SQL scripts, code, or images.
    • @ Table mentions: Autocomplete table names to pre-load schema context.
    • Folder icon: Link files directly from existing projects or artifacts.
    • Mode toggle: Switch between Flash and Deep analytical engines.
    • Voice waveform icon: Launch Resona Voice instantly right from the input bar.

2 — Choose Flash or Deep¶

Flash works fast and gives you the answer directly. Deep does the same work with more time on it — thinking longer and following the question across tables and wider schema instead of stopping at the first answer.

You can switch at any point; it applies from your next message.

3 — Ask Your Question¶

Type it however you'd ask a colleague:

"Show me the top 10 customers by revenue this quarter"
"What's the 30-day retention for users who signed up in Q1 vs Q2?"

  • Mention a table with @ to save Resona a step — pick from the list and it starts with that table already in context.

resona-ai/dashboard.content:
Resona Dashboard AI¶

Resona Dashboard AI is your dedicated live dashboard analytics and visualization partner. Anchored beside your database dashboards, it transforms complex relational data into intuitive visual cards, runs autonomous multi-query diagnostic loops, and lets you craft or refine business dashboards entirely through conversation.

Quick links: Dashboard Guide · Resona AI Chat · Memory Settings

1 — What Dashboard AI Can Do¶

Rather than requiring you to hand-craft SQL aggregations or manually drag BI widgets, Dashboard AI handles the entire analytics lifecycle:

  • Generate Full Dashboards: Analyzes your database and builds complete, thematic dashboards with KPI cards, growth curves, cohort grids, and distribution charts.
  • Modify in Place: Add new cards, drop obsolete panels, change grouping dimensions, or adjust chart types conversationally.
  • Surface Executive Recommendations: Generates Executive Read cards that pair headline metrics with plain-English diagnoses and concrete tactical next steps.
  • Diagnose Anomalies: Ask why a metric dropped or spiked, and Dashboard AI will write and run targeted SQL queries to pinpoint the root cause.
  • Keyboard Shortcut: Press Ctrl / Cmd + J anywhere in Dashboard mode to instantly toggle the Dashboard AI panel.

Example Prompts¶

Get started immediately with the quick suggestion chips or type your own instructions:

"What are our primary revenue drivers and growth trends?"
"Summarize overall business health and customer retention"
"Highlight key executive KPIs and weekly performance"
"Add a breakdown of active learners by school board and grade level"
"Why did signups dip in the first week of September?"

2 — Autonomous Multi-Query Execution¶

When asked to generate or update a dashboard, Resona Dashboard AI doesn't guess column names or generate static mockups. It executes an autonomous, multi-step agentic plan:

The Agentic Loop¶

  1. Get Schema Context: Resona introspects your active PostgreSQL tables, data types, primary keys, foreign-key relationships, and enum definitions.
  2. Planned Query Batches: The AI plans an optimal set of analytical queries (e.g. Ran 13 queries), grouping calculations by business domain.
  3. Query Database Trace: Each database probe executes through your local Connector in strictly read-only mode. You can expand the trace to inspect individual SQL queries, execution latency, and row results.
  4. Card & Layout Assembly: The AI formats the results into appropriate visualization types (line charts, area trends, donut breakdowns, or narrative cards) and mounts them into your active dashboard.

3 — File & Document Attachments¶

Dashboard AI is multimodal. Using the + Attach button beside the prompt bar, you can upload external reference documents directly into your conversation:

Supported File Types:¶

  • Spreadsheets (.csv, .xlsx, .xls): Upload partner sales exports, offline expense spreadsheets, or legacy BI dumps.
  • Documents (.pdf, .docx, .txt, .md): Attach quarterly business reviews, KPI requirement briefs, or investor decks.
  • Code & Database Scripts (.sql, .ts, .py, .json): Provide existing SQL scripts, Prisma/Drizzle schemas, or configuration objects.
  • Images (.png, .jpg, .webp): Attach wireframes, design mockups, or chart screenshots to guide the visual styling.

Practical Use Cases:¶

  • Reconcile Discrepancies: Upload a Stripe or Shopify CSV report and ask Dashboard AI to match it against your internal orders and subscriptions database tables.
  • Implement Business Briefs: Upload a product manager's requirements PDF and ask: "Build the executive dashboard specified on page 3 of this document."
  • Replicate Dashboards: Upload a screenshot of a legacy dashboard from another tool and ask Dashboard AI to rebuild it using your current PostgreSQL schema.

4 — Analytical Modes: Deep vs. Flash¶

Dashboard AI provides two distinct execution modes, with Deep mode active by default:

ModeCharacteristicsWhen to Use
Deep (Default)Multi-turn reasoning, multi-table joins, cross-schema correlation, statistical variance analysis, and written executive recommendations.Comprehensive dashboard generation, anomaly root-cause investigation, and cohort analysis.
FlashUltra-fast single-turn execution, direct table queries, minimal credit usage.Quick layout edits, renaming cards, changing chart colors, or simple scalar lookups.

Switch between modes anytime using the dropdown selector in the bottom input bar.

5 — Initial Dashboard Generation¶

When you connect a database that has no dashboard defined yet, Dashboard AI presents a clear onboarding roadmap:

  1. Structure Understanding: AI maps table relationships and data models automatically.
  2. Metric Identification: AI identifies primary metrics, revenue streams, and behavioral cohorts.
  3. Read-Only Safety: Strictly isolated queries ensure production data is never touched or modified.
  4. Executive Synthesis: Translates raw rows into high-level KPIs and strategic narratives.
  5. Interactive Delivery: Generates a persistent dashboard you and your team can interact with.

6 — Memory & Context Continuity¶

Dashboard AI is backed by Schema Weaver's Memory System. It maintains context across conversation turns and remembers:

  • Previously generated cards and layout customizations.
  • Custom business metrics and domain formulas defined during earlier sessions.
  • Pinned terminology and specific table filters.

If you refresh your browser or return tomorrow, Dashboard AI picks up right where you left off.

Next Steps¶

  • Statistics & Metrics with AI — interactive card operations, resizing, and focus mode
  • Resona AI Chat — ad-hoc conversational querying and table exports
  • Memory Settings — manage persistent agent memory and business facts
  • The Connector — local credential boundary and query execution architecture

resona-ai.content:
Resona AI¶

Resona is Schema Weaver's AI assistant. In the Data Explorer it works your live database, and it comes in four forms that share the same memory. It also appears in the SQL Editor, where it works on your schema instead.

Same account, same credit pool across all of it.

In the Data Explorer¶

FormWhat it's for
ChatAsk questions in plain English, get written reports and exports
VoiceAsk out loud instead of typing
DashboardBuild an executive dashboard of KPIs, trends, cohorts and insights
MemoryWhat Resona carries forward between conversations

They share one memory, so a metric definition you set in chat is already known to the dashboard and to voice.

How it works¶

Resona writes and runs its own SQL. One tool executes queries and the model does the analysis inside that SQL, so the approach fits your question rather than being fixed in advance. Queries are read-only, run against a single database, and are checked by the Connector before they reach it.

It plans its own work and recovers from its own mistakes — if a query fails, it works out why and changes something rather than retrying blindly.

In the SQL Editor¶

Resona also works on your schema. It reads your project files, reasons over your compiled schema graph and ER diagram, makes targeted multi-file edits, and applies migrations — from a conversation.

→ Resona AI in the SQL Editor

Which one to use¶

Data ExplorerSQL Editor
Works withLive database rowsSchema definitions and project files
ProducesAnswers, written reports, exportsSQL DDL, file edits, migration scripts
Database neededYesOnly for migrations and drift
Changes anythingNo — read-onlyYes — writes files, applies migrations
Visual outputDashboards, voiceNone

Use the Data Explorer to query and understand live data. Use the SQL Editor to design and evolve the schema behind it.

Shared Credits¶

Credits are shared across both surfaces — a conversation in the SQL Editor and a query in the Data Explorer both draw from the same monthly pool. Use Resona wherever it's most useful without managing separate budgets.

Plan details and credit costs live in Plans and Credits.

Getting Started¶

In the Data Explorer

  1. Open data-explorer.schemaweaver.dev
  2. Select a database connection
  3. Ask a question — or press the voice orb and ask out loud

→ Chat Interface

In the SQL Editor

  1. Open sql-editor.schemaweaver.dev
  2. Open a project and click Resona AI in the left sidebar
  3. Ask anything about your schema

→ Resona AI in the SQL Editor

Next Steps¶

  • Resona Voice — talking instead of typing
  • Resona Dashboard — metrics over time
  • Memory — what Resona remembers, and how to change it
  • Plans and Credits — plans, monthly pools, and what things cost

resona-ai/memory.content:
AI Memory¶

AI Memory is Schema Weaver's shared knowledge system. As you chat, talk, or build dashboards, Resona automatically captures business directives, table relationships, and custom metric definitions into a persistent markdown knowledge base.

Open memory anytime from Settings → AI Memory.

Quick links: Chat Interface · Resona Voice · Dashboard AI · Plans & Credits

1 — One Shared Memory Across All 3 Agents¶

Memory is unified across all three AI surfaces. Any definition established or corrected in one agent is immediately known to the other two:

Agent SurfaceHow It Uses Shared Memory
Resona AI ChatAccurately joins custom tables and filters calculations without needing repetitive instructions in prompt messages.
Resona VoiceSpeaks answers informed by your business context, interpreting verbal shorthand like "active learners" or "habitual usage" correctly.
Resona Dashboard AIAssembles executive cards, KPI metrics, and growth charts adhering to your exact formulas and founder rules.

Teach Resona how your revenue or user status is computed once, and every conversation across chat, audio, and visual dashboards builds upon that knowledge.

2 — Automatic Memory Generation Through Conversation¶

You don't need to manually draft configuration files before using Schema Weaver:

  • Built Conversationally: As you ask questions and explore tables, Resona autonomously extracts business facts, domain rules, and table conventions from your interactions.
  • Categorized Sections:
    • Founder Directives: High-level structural rules and presentation constraints (e.g., The Executive Analysis section should present KPI and insight cards only, with no charts).
    • Metric Definitions: Concrete SQL business logic and column mappings (e.g., how tutor_correction_rate or chat_habit is calculated).
    • Table Nuances & Quirks: Important notes about soft deletes, legacy columns, or tenant isolation columns.
  • Timestamped & Traceable: Directives include the date they were established, making it easy to track how definitions evolve.

3 — Direct In-Place Editing (Click to Edit)¶

Memory belongs entirely to you. You can review, refine, or rewrite anything the AI has recorded directly in the UI:

  • Click to Edit: The memory view is an active markdown surface. Click anywhere on the text to open the in-place editor (Click to edit tooltip), make your adjustments, and click Save.
  • Two Memory Scopes:
    • Database (MEMORY.md): Scoped to the selected database connection (e.g., cloopdb). Shared across team members who connect to that same database.

# AI Memory

**AI Memory** is Schema Weaver's shared knowledge system. As you chat, talk, or build dashboards, Resona automatically captures business directives, table relationships, and custom metric definitions into a persistent markdown knowledge base.

Open memory anytime from **Settings → AI Memory**.

![Resona AI Memory settings panel showing Database Memory with Founder Directives, Metric Definitions, and inline click-to-edit surface](/images/de/resona-ai/memeory/overview.png)

> Quick links: [Chat Interface](/resona-ai/ai-chat) · [Resona Voice](/resona-ai/voice) · [Dashboard AI](/resona-ai/dashboard) · [Plans & Credits](/pricing)

---

## 1 — One Shared Memory Across All 3 Agents

Memory is unified across all three AI surfaces. Any definition established or corrected in one agent is immediately known to the other two:

| Agent Surface | How It Uses Shared Memory |
|---|---|
| **[Resona AI Chat](/resona-ai/ai-chat)** | Accurately joins custom tables and filters calculations without needing repetitive instructions in prompt messages. |
| **[Resona Voice](/resona-ai/voice)** | Speaks answers informed by your business context, interpreting verbal shorthand like *"active learners"* or *"habitual usage"* correctly. |
| **[Resona Dashboard AI](/resona-ai/dashboard)** | Assembles executive cards, KPI metrics, and growth charts adhering to your exact formulas and founder rules. |

Teach Resona how your revenue or user status is computed once, and every conversation across chat, audio, and visual dashboards builds upon that knowledge.

---

## 2 — Automatic Memory Generation Through Conversation

You don't need to manually draft configuration files before using Schema Weaver:

- **Built Conversationally**: As you ask questions and explore tables, Resona autonomously extracts business facts, domain rules, and table conventions from your interactions.
- **Categorized Sections**:
  - **Founder Directives**: High-level structural rules and presentation constraints (e.g., `The Executive Analysis section should present KPI and insight cards only, with no charts`).
  - **Metric Definitions**: Concrete SQL business logic and column mappings (e.g., how `tutor_correction_rate` or `chat_habit` is calculated).
  - **Table Nuances & Quirks**: Important notes about soft deletes, legacy columns, or tenant isolation columns.
- **Timestamped & Traceable**: Directives include the date they were established, making it easy to track how definitions evolve.

---

## 3 — Direct In-Place Editing (Click to Edit)

Memory belongs entirely to you. You can review, refine, or rewrite anything the AI has recorded directly in the UI:

- **Click to Edit**: The memory view is an active markdown surface. Click anywhere on the text to open the in-place editor (`Click to edit` tooltip), make your adjustments, and click **Save**.
- **Two Memory Scopes**:
  - **Database (`MEMORY.md`)**: Scoped to the selected database connection (e.g., `cloopdb`). Shared across team members who connect to that same database.
  - **Profile (`USER_PROFILE.md`)**: Scoped to your individual user account. Holds personal preferences and analytical habits across all databases.
- **Recompile from Live Schema**: Click the recompile button (`RotateCcw`) to refresh and synchronize memory with your latest database schema migrations.
- **One-Click Copy**: Use the copy button to export your database's memory markdown for internal team documentation or pull requests.

---

- [Resona Dashboard AI](/resona-ai/dashboard) — executive dashboard generation and metric cards

resona-ai/voice.content:
Resona Voice¶

Resona Voice is Schema Weaver's conversational voice data analyst. Speak to your database naturally out loud — Resona listens, introspects your schema, queries your PostgreSQL tables through the local read-only connector, and speaks answers back to you in real time without requiring manual SQL writing or keyboard typing.

Quick links: Chat Interface · Resona Dashboard AI · Exploring Data · Memory

1 — Starting a Voice Session¶

You can start a Resona Voice session from anywhere in the application:

Direct Launch from Resona AI Input Bar¶

Inside the Resona AI Chat panel, look at the right side of the prompt input bar:

  • Click the audio waveform button (tooltip: Start Resona Voice) or the microphone button.
  • Your session initializes immediately without navigating away from your active work.
  • You can also toggle Voice anytime using the global keyboard shortcut Ctrl / Cmd + K.

2 — The Connection & Orb Lifecycle¶

When a voice session begins, Resona establishes a low-latency, bidirectional audio stream. The dynamic orb reflects the agent's real-time state:

Orb StateColor & IndicatorWhat's Happening
ConnectingAmber pulsing orb (Connecting...)Establishing secure WebRTC / WebSocket audio channel
ListeningAquatic green/teal pulsing wavesCapturing your spoken words via microphone
ThinkingShimmering violet/blue orbIntrospecting schema, formulating SQL queries, and analyzing row results
SpeakingActive teal concentric rippleStreaming synthesized spoken response and updating live speech bubbles
IdleCalming steady glowWaiting for you or colleague to speak

3 — Ambient & Persistent: Minimized Everywhere¶

A voice session is never trapped inside a single tab or dialog. When minimized, Resona Voice transforms into a compact, floating ambient companion that travels with you across every view in Schema Weaver.

Floating on the Data Explorer Grid¶

Inspect raw records while conversing with your analyst:

  • Navigate tables, scroll through 500 / 1k / 2k rows, apply instant in-memory filters, or open full JSON/text inspection popovers.
  • Speak aloud: "What is the distribution of message types in this table?" or "Which user has the most records here?"
  • Resona queries the database in the background and answers into your headphones while your eyes stay focused on the grid.

Floating on the Executive Dashboard¶

Examine high-level metrics with voice-driven drill-downs:

  • Drag to Move: Hover over the widget (Click to expand · Drag to move) and drag it anywhere on screen so it never obstructs your charts, KPI cards, or cohort graphs.
  • One-Click Mute: Click the red mic icon to instantly mute your microphone while keeping the audio session alive.
  • Expand Anytime: Click the expand icon (⤢) to bring back the full-screen conversation view and transcript history.
  • Ask questions about live visuals: "Why did the daily average score dip on September 16?" or "Which subject has the highest accuracy?"

4 — Conversational Experience & Capabilities¶

Resona Voice is engineered to converse like an experienced colleague rather than a robotic text-to-speech engine:

  • Natural Spoken Answers: Resona synthesizes findings into concise, clear takeaways. It will never read raw row dumps or verbose SQL syntax at you over audio.
  • Barge-In Interruptibility: You can interrupt at any moment. The instant you speak, Resona immediately stops talking, listens to your correction, and adjusts course.
  • Temporal & Relative Awareness: The current timestamp is always part of the context window. Phrases like "last Tuesday", "this past quarter", or "year-to-date" resolve to exact SQL date ranges automatically.
  • Web & Domain Context: If a query involves external context (such as industry benchmarks or public exchange rates), Voice can fetch live reference data.
  • Session Memory: Checks your connection's Memory Dossier for saved KPI definitions, table aliases, and business rules.

5 — Voice Controls & Keyboard Mode¶

The floating voice control bar provides complete hands-free and hybrid control:

ControlAction
+ TypeOpens a quick inline keyboard input to type numbers, spelling corrections, or specific email addresses without hanging up the call.
Microphone ButtonToggles voice recording on or off.
Mute / UnmuteQuick-mute toggle available directly on the minimized floating orb.
Expand (⤢) / MinimizeSwitches between full conversation mode with transcript bubbles and ambient floating orb.
End Session (X / Power)Safely terminates the audio connection and concludes credit tracking. You can also simply say "Goodbye" or "End call".

6 — Credit Usage¶

Voice interactions draw from your standard unified credit pool:

  • Credits are metered transparently per conversational turn (visible on each message bubble, e.g. 29 credits used, 269 credits used).
  • Voice queries share the exact same quota with Resona AI Chat and Dashboard AI.
  • If your account reaches its monthly credit threshold, the session gently pauses and alerts you to top up or switch to manual grid browsing.

When to Use Voice vs. Chat¶

CapabilityResona VoiceResona AI Chat
Best ForFast exploratory questions, hands-free drill-downs while looking at charts or gridsFormal executive reports, downloadable exports, complex schema refactoring
InteractionHands-free natural speech, barge-in interruptsKeyboard prompt, @ table mentions, + file uploads
OutputNatural spoken audio + live transcript bubblesRich markdown tables, charts, CSV / Excel / PDF exports
PresenceAmbient floating orb (minimized across Grid & Dashboard)Dedicated workspace and side copilot panel

Next Steps¶

  • Chat Interface — text questions, @ table mentions, and file uploads
  • Resona Dashboard AI — generating executive dashboards and metric cards
  • Exploring Your Data — using the high-performance table grid
  • Memory Settings — managing saved terminology and custom formulas

resona-ai/workspace.content:
Workspace & Projects¶

Resona keeps what it generates. The Workspace holds your generated files, Projects group related conversations together, and Artifact History gives you a searchable archive of everything produced so far.

Workspace¶

The Workspace is a persistent store for the reports and exports Resona produces. Open it from the workspace icon in the AI panel toolbar.

What's in it¶

FormatBest for
PDFPrinted reports, email attachments
HTMLBrowser-based sharing, embedded reports
CSVRaw result sets, further processing
ExcelFormatted workbooks

Managing files¶

Each file can be downloaded, renamed, and deleted. If Resona regenerates a report in the same session, both versions are kept.

Files are scoped to the Project that was active when they were created. If you aren't using Projects, everything goes into the default workspace.

Projects¶

A Project groups related conversations and their outputs under one name — so when you're investigating something specific, everything about it stays together.

A project contains:

  • The chat sessions assigned to it
  • The Workspace files generated in those sessions
  • The artifacts from those sessions
  • A colour and icon you choose for quick recognition

Open the Projects panel from the sidebar, click New Project, and name it. Select the project before or after starting a chat to assign it, and move a chat between projects at any time from the chat options menu.

Artifact History¶

Every table, report, and file Resona has produced — across all sessions and projects — is searchable here.

Filter by the text of the original question, the artefact type, a date range, or a specific project.

From any entry you can reopen it in its full interactive view, copy the SQL behind it, jump back to the conversation that produced it, or pin it to your dashboard.

That last one is useful when you remember an analysis from weeks ago but can't remember which chat it was in.

Next Steps¶

  • Resona AI — what the agent can do
  • Exporting Data — taking data out of the grid
  • Data Explorer — back to the overview

team-collaboration.content:
Team Collaboration¶

Collaboration in Schema Weaver is built around teams. Create a team, invite your colleagues, share your local agent connectors, and collaborate on shared AI projects and databases — with zero credential exposure.

Quick links: Plans & Credits · Connector Sharing · Security Architecture

1 — Collaboration Hub (Settings → Collaboration)¶

Open Settings → Collaboration to access your team control center:

  • Active Team Switcher: Switch between organizations or create a new team anytime using + New Team.
  • Your Permission: Clear indicator of your team authority (Owner, Admin, or Member).
  • Seat Quotas & Limits: Displays current seat usage (e.g., Seats 2/2). If your seat capacity is reached, an alert prompts the team owner to upgrade on Plans & Credits before sending additional invites.
  • Four Core Sub-Tabs:
    1. Members: Invite colleagues and manage member roles.
    2. Connectors: Share or unshare local connectors.
    3. Share Projects: Distribute AI workspaces and saved chats.
    4. Shared DBs: View all team-accessible databases.

2 — Members & Role Management¶

Under the Members tab, owners and admins can invite new teammates and govern permissions:

Inviting Teammates¶

  1. Enter your colleague's corporate email address (colleague@company.com).
  2. Select their role (Member by default, or Admin).
  3. Click Invite.

If the invited person does not yet have a Schema Weaver account, the email invite guides them through account setup. No pre-existing account is required.

Roles and Permissions¶

RoleWhat They Can Do
OwnerFull authority — manage billing, upgrade seat counts, invite and remove members, change roles, share/disconnect projects and connectors, and delete the team.
AdminManage team members, pending invitations, projects, and shared connectors. Cannot alter subscription billing or delete the team.
MemberBrowse shared databases in the Data Explorer, run read-only queries, converse with Resona AI, and participate in shared AI projects.

3 — Sharing Connectors¶

Under the Connectors tab, you can grant team members access to databases reaching through your local Connector daemon:

  • One-Click Share/Unshare: Toggle whether your registered connector daemon (e.g. vivek-laptop-msi) is shared with the active team.
  • Agent Identity & Health: Displays the unique agent ID (agt_vivek-laptop-msi_12662b69) and a live heartbeat indicator (green status dot) showing whether the daemon is online.
  • Zero Credential Sharing: Teammates receive tunnel access to execute read-only queries through your connector, but your database passwords, hosts, and secrets never leave your machine.

→ Learn more in Sharing with Your Team.

4 — Sharing AI Projects¶

Under the Share Projects tab, team members can collaborate on conversational analyses, dashboards, and research workspaces:

  • Project Workspaces: Select any private project (e.g., cloop-dataset General Workspace) and click Share with Team.
  • Collaborative History: Once shared, teammates can review conversation history, inspect generated artifacts, re-run queries, and build on existing analyses without duplicating effort.
  • Unified Memory: Directives and metric definitions saved in the project's memory dossier become immediately accessible to all team members using Resona AI, Resona Voice, and Dashboard AI.

5 — Browsing Shared Databases¶

Under the Shared DBs tab, team members can see every database currently accessible to the team:

  • Centralized Inventory: Shows all databases currently tunneled through shared connectors (e.g., migration-engine-testing, schema-weaver, sw-analytics, postgres, cloopdb).
  • Live Status & Agent Provenance: Each card shows an active online status indicator, the host daemon machine name, and an AGENT badge.
  • Instant Availability: Any database listed here immediately appears in the Data Explorer connection dropdown for all team members.

6 — Seats and Billing Governance¶

On paid plans, seats govern team capacity:

OwnerAdminMember
Invite & Remove Members✓✓—
Change Member Roles✓✓—
Share & Unshare Connectors✓✓—
Share & Unlink Projects✓✓—
Manage Seats & Billing✓——
Delete Team✓——
  • The Team Plan includes a two-seat base ($30/mo) with each additional seat at $15/mo.
  • Each seat receives its own dedicated 100,000 monthly credits pool and 10,000 daily cap, ensuring one teammate's queries never exhaust another teammate's quota.

Next Steps¶

  • Plans and Credits — seat pricing, monthly credit pools, and daily caps
  • Sharing with Your Team — deep dive into connector sharing mechanics
  • Security Architecture — how credentials stay safe on your local machine
  • Workspace & Projects — organizing AI chats and generated reports

### Inviting Teammates

1. Enter your colleague's corporate email address (`colleague@company.com`).
2. Select their role (**Member** by default, or **Admin**).
3. Click **Invite**. 

If the invited person does not yet have a Schema Weaver account, the email invite guides them through account setup. No pre-existing account is required.

### Roles and Permissions

| Role | What They Can Do |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | Full authority — manage billing, upgrade seat counts, invite and remove members, change roles, share/disconnect projects and connectors, and delete the team. |
| **Admin** | Manage team members, pending invitations, projects, and shared connectors. Cannot alter subscription billing or delete the team. |
| **Member** | Browse shared databases in the Data Explorer, run read-only queries, converse with Resona AI, and participate in shared AI projects. |

---

## 3 — Sharing Connectors

Under the **`Connectors`** tab, you can grant team members access to databases reaching through your local Connector daemon:

![Collaboration Connectors tab displaying active local connector with shared status and unshare button](/images/de/team/sharing-connecots.png)

- **One-Click Share/Unshare**: Toggle whether your registered connector daemon (e.g. `vivek-laptop-msi`) is shared with the active team.
- **Agent Identity & Health**: Displays the unique agent ID (`agt_vivek-laptop-msi_12662b69`) and a live heartbeat indicator (green status dot) showing whether the daemon is online.
- **Zero Credential Sharing**: Teammates receive tunnel access to execute read-only queries through your connector, but your database passwords, hosts, and secrets **never leave your machine**.

→ Learn more in [Sharing with Your Team](/connector/sharing).

---

## 4 — Sharing AI Projects

Under the **`Share Projects`** tab, team members can collaborate on conversational analyses, dashboards, and research workspaces:

![Collaboration Share Projects tab showing AI Projects like cloop-dataset with Share with Team action](/images/de/team/ai-rproject-sharing.png)

- **Project Workspaces**: Select any private project (e.g., `cloop-dataset` General Workspace) and click **Share with Team**.
- **Collaborative History**: Once shared, teammates can review conversation history, inspect generated artifacts, re-run queries, and build on existing analyses without duplicating effort.
- **Unified Memory**: Directives and metric definitions saved in the project's memory dossier become immediately accessible to all team members using [Resona AI](/resona-ai), [Resona Voice](/resona-ai/voice), and [Dashboard AI](/resona-ai/dashboard).

---

## 5 — Browsing Shared Databases

Under the **`Shared DBs`** tab, team members can see every database currently accessible to the team:

![Collaboration Shared DBs tab displaying all 5 shared databases accessible via local connectors with live status indicators](/images/de/team/db-sharing.png)

- **Centralized Inventory**: Shows all databases currently tunneled through shared connectors (e.g., `migration-engine-testing`, `schema-weaver`, `sw-analytics`, `postgres`, `cloopdb`).
- **Live Status & Agent Provenance**: Each card shows an active online status indicator, the host daemon machine name, and an `AGENT` badge.
- **Instant Availability**: Any database listed here immediately appears in the Data Explorer connection dropdown for all team members.

---

## 6 — Seats and Billing Governance

On paid plans, seats govern team capacity:

| | Owner | Admin | Member |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Invite & Remove Members** | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| **Change Member Roles** | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| **Share & Unshare Connectors** | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| **Share & Unlink Projects** | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| **Manage Seats & Billing** | ✓ | — | — |
| **Delete Team** | ✓ | — | — |

- The **Team Plan** includes a **two-seat base** ($30/mo) with each additional seat at $15/mo.
- Each seat receives its own dedicated **100,000 monthly credits** pool and **10,000 daily cap**, ensuring one teammate's queries never exhaust another teammate's quota.

---

## Next Steps

- [Plans and Credits](/pricing) — seat pricing, monthly credit pools, and daily caps
- [Sharing with Your Team](/connector/sharing) — deep dive into connector sharing mechanics
- [Security Architecture](/connector/security-architecture) — how credentials stay safe on your local machine
- [Workspace & Projects](/resona-ai/workspace) — organizing AI chats and generated reports

Plans and Credits¶

Three plans: Free, Pro, and Team. Resona works the same way on all of them — the difference is how many credits you get and what you can share with a team.

Quick links: Pricing Page · Contact Sales

Plans¶

PlanPriceCredits / monthDaily cap
Free$03,000None
Pro$29 / mo200,00020,000
Team$30 / mo (2 seats)100,000 per seat10,000 per seat

Team is priced per seat¶

The Team plan bills $15 per seat, with a two-seat base — so $30 covers the first two people, and each additional seat is $15.

Seats are how many people can use the workspace. Your subscription shows how many are in use and how many remain, and owners can add or remove seats from the team billing settings.

What each plan includes¶

FreeProTeam
AI credits3,000 / mo200,000 / mo100,000 per seat
Daily capNone20,00010,000 per seat
Flash & Deep modes✓✓✓
Voice AI (speech queries)✓✓✓
Team membersJoin by inviteUp to 5By seat
Shared database connections✓✓✓
SupportCommunityPriorityPriority

Pro includes team sharing for up to 5 people, but each member's credits are their own — there's no shared pool.

Team is what makes the workspace genuinely collaborative: connections and workspaces are shared across everyone on the team. Credits are still per seat here too, so each person gets their own 100,000 rather than drawing from one shared balance.

What credits are¶

Credits are what Resona costs to run. Every message, query, and generated report draws from the balance, and all of your surfaces — chat, voice, and dashboards — draw from the same one.

Free has no daily cap: the whole 3,000 is available whenever you want it. Every plan resets at the start of the billing month, and unused credits don't carry over.

Monitoring credit usage (Settings → AI Usage)¶

To check your current credit consumption, remaining balances, and daily resets, navigate to the AI Usage panel in the Settings menu:

  1. Click the gear icon or your profile avatar in the bottom-left sidebar to open Settings.
  2. Select AI Usage from the left-hand navigation.

Key metrics tracked:¶

  • Monthly credits — Displays total credits consumed in the current billing cycle against your monthly allowance (e.g., 364 / 100K credits, 0% used, 99.6K credits remaining), along with a breakdown of credits used today.
  • Daily safety cap — Displays today's usage against your plan's daily limit (e.g., 364 / 10K credits, 4% used, 9.6K credits remaining) alongside a live countdown timer until daily quota reset (e.g., Resets in 12h 50m).
  • Concurrent agents — Reflects active parallel execution capacity (e.g., 0 / 2), indicating how many simultaneous agentic workflows can run in parallel.
  • Plan tier — Identifies your active subscription tier (Team, Pro, or Free).
  • Live refresh — Click the refresh icon in the top header anytime to get up-to-the-minute credit metrics.

Next Steps¶

  • Resona AI — what you're spending credits on
  • AI Memory — shared knowledge system and directives
  • Team Collaboration — sharing with your team

# Plans and Credits

Three plans: **Free**, **Pro**, and **Team**. Resona works the same way on all of them — the difference is how many credits you get and what you can share with a team.

> Quick links: [Pricing Page](https://schemaweaver.dev/pricing) · [Contact Sales](mailto:support@schemaweaver.dev)

---

## Plans

| Plan | Price | Credits / month | Daily cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | **$0** | 3,000 | None |
| **Pro** | **$29 / mo** | 200,000 | 20,000 |
| **Team** | **$30 / mo** (2 seats) | 100,000 per seat | 10,000 per seat |

---

## Team is priced per seat

The Team plan bills **$15 per seat**, with a **two-seat base** — so $30 covers the first two people, and each additional seat is $15.

Seats are how many people can use the workspace. Your subscription shows how many are in use and how many remain, and owners can add or remove seats from the team billing settings.

---

## What each plan includes

| | Free | Pro | Team |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AI credits** | 3,000 / mo | 200,000 / mo | 100,000 per seat |
| **Daily cap** | None | 20,000 | 10,000 per seat |
| **Flash & Deep modes** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Voice AI (speech queries)** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Team members** | Join by invite | Up to 5 | By seat |
| **Shared database connections** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Support** | Community | Priority | Priority |

**Pro** includes team sharing for up to 5 people, but each member's credits are their own — there's no shared pool.

**Team** is what makes the workspace genuinely collaborative: connections and workspaces are shared across everyone on the team. Credits are still **per seat** here too, so each person gets their own 100,000 rather than drawing from one shared balance.

---

## What credits are

Credits are what Resona costs to run. Every message, query, and generated report draws from the balance, and all of your surfaces — chat, voice, and dashboards — draw from the same one.

**Free** has no daily cap: the whole 3,000 is available whenever you want it. Every plan resets at the start of the billing month, and unused credits don't carry over.

---

## Monitoring credit usage (`Settings → AI Usage`)

To check your current credit consumption, remaining balances, and daily resets, navigate to the **AI Usage** panel in the Settings menu:

1. Click the gear icon or your profile avatar in the bottom-left sidebar to open **Settings**.
2. Select **AI Usage** from the left-hand navigation.

![Schema Weaver Settings showing AI Credit Usage with monthly and daily progress bars, concurrent agents capacity, and plan tier](/images/de/resona-ai/ussage-ai-credit.png)

### Key metrics tracked:

- **Monthly credits** — Displays total credits consumed in the current billing cycle against your monthly allowance (e.g., `364 / 100K credits`, `0% used`, `99.6K credits remaining`), along with a breakdown of credits used today.
- **Daily safety cap** — Displays today's usage against your plan's daily limit (e.g., `364 / 10K credits`, `4% used`, `9.6K credits remaining`) alongside a live countdown timer until daily quota reset (e.g., `Resets in 12h 50m`).
- **Concurrent agents** — Reflects active parallel execution capacity (e.g., `0 / 2`), indicating how many simultaneous agentic workflows can run in parallel.
- **Plan tier** — Identifies your active subscription tier (`Team`, `Pro`, or `Free`).
- **Live refresh** — Click the refresh icon in the top header anytime to get up-to-the-minute credit metrics.

---
